initial_observation.demographics: A 64-year-old woman who had a liver transplant 18 months earlier for autoimmune hepatitis and was on mycophenolate and tacrolimus
initial_observation.encounter_context: Presented with neurological symptoms prompting initial diagnostic workup
initial_observation.chief_complaint: A week of generalized weakness, headaches, confusion, and disorientation
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: Patient was confused. Fundoscopic examination revealed papilledema. Neurological evaluation showed left-sided hemiparesis, left-sided sensory changes, left-sided pyramidal signs, visuospatial deficits, and loss of sensation on the right side of the body. Laboratory tests including CRP and ESR were normal; elevated gamma-glutamyl transferase and platelet counts; negative CMV IgM, Hepatitis B & C, HIV, Toxoplasma gondii, and CMV IgG. Initial brain CT without contrast showed absence of hemorrhage.
presenting_symptoms: loss of sensation on right side of the body
known_prior_history: Liver transplant 18 months ago for autoimmune hepatitis
Immunosuppressive therapy with mycophenolate and tacrolimus

evidence_items.source_text: an MRI scan was ordered, revealing multiple ring-enhancing lesions, primarily located in the right frontal lobe, temporoparietal regions, and left parietal lobe, with the largest measuring 2.7 cm in maximal diameter. These lesions were associated with moderate vasogenic edema.

The brain biopsy revealed diffuse infiltrates of closely packed intermediate to large mononuclear cells with scant cytoplasm. Additionally, a perivascular infiltrate composed of atypical lymphoid cells and a widespread infiltrate of neoplastic intermediate to large lymphocytes tested positive for the B-cell marker CD20.
evidence_items.temporal_cue: after urgent craniotomy and brain biopsy

evidence_items.source_text: The patient was diagnosed with CNS PTLD, specifically high-grade diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) of the activated B-cell phenotype.
